title: Single-Row Keyboard
statement:
A special keyboard has all 26 letter keys in one row. The string `keyboard` gives the layout: the key at index `i` (counting from `0`) types the letter `keyboard[i]`.

You type with a single finger that starts above index `0`. To type a letter, the finger moves to that letter's key; going from index `i` to index `j` takes `|i - j|` units of time, and pressing a key costs nothing more. Return the total time needed to type the string `word`, one letter after another.
constraints: keyboard contains every lowercase English letter exactly once, in some order
word contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The time is just the sum of the distances between consecutive finger positions, starting at index 0. The only work is finding where each letter sits. Searching `keyboard` for every letter of `word` costs up to 26 steps per letter; building a letter-to-index lookup once makes every search a single hash lookup.

## Approach

1. Build `position`, mapping each letter of `keyboard` to its index.
2. Start with `time = 0` and the finger at `current = 0`.
3. For each `letter` of `word`, look up its `index`, add `|index - current|` to `time`, and move the finger there.
4. Return `time`.

## Example 1, step by step

`keyboard = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"`, `word = "cba"`. The finger starts at 0. `'c'` is at index 2: `time = 2`, `current = 2`. `'b'` is at index 1: `time = 3`, `current = 1`. `'a'` is at index 0: `time = 4`. The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(26 + m) for a word of length m: one pass to build the map, one pass over the word.
- Space: O(26) = O(1) for the map.

## Pitfalls

- The finger starts at index 0, not at the first letter of `word`; typing the first letter can already cost time.
- Use the absolute difference: the finger moves both left and right.
- Repeating the same letter costs 0, so do not add a fixed cost per key press.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `position` | map from each letter to its index on the keyboard |
| `time` | total movement so far |
| `current` | index the finger is above |
| `letter` | the letter being typed |
| `index` | where `letter` sits on the keyboard |

narration.2: This map will answer 'where is this letter?' in one step.
narration.4: Remember that keyboard[i] sits at index i.
narration.6: No time has been spent yet.
narration.8: Type the word one letter at a time.
narration.9: Look up where the letter's key is.
narration.10: Moving the finger costs the distance between the two indices, in either direction.
narration.11: The finger now rests on this key.
narration.13: The accumulated distance is the total typing time.
